chunks: Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan al-Ṣaffār, from al-Ḥasan ibn Mūsā al-Khashshāb, from Ghiyāth ibn Kallūb, from Isḥāq ibn ʿAmmār, from Abū Jaʿfar, from his father, peace be upon them, that ʿAlī, peace be upon him, used to say:
The intentional act of children is treated as a mistake; the ʿāqilah bears it.

key_terms.الْعَاقِلَةُ: the legally responsible male kin group who bear blood-money liability
key_terms.تَحْمِلُهُ: bears it or assumes liability for it
key_terms.خَطَأٌ: a mistaken or accidental act in legal classification

ai.seo_question: In Shia fiqh, who bears liability when a child intentionally causes harm?
ai.summary: This hadith states a legal ruling concerning the liability of minors. It establishes that the deliberate harmful act of a child is legally treated as accidental, and the financial liability is borne by the ʿāqilah rather than the child himself.
